Definition: from G164; to make captive:--lead away captive, bring into captivity.
BiblicalUsage: Luke uses it of Jerusalem's people led away captive into all nations, and Paul uses it of the war inside himself — sin's law bringing him into captivity to the law of sin. Twice it turns hopeful: believers take every thought captive to the obedience of Christ, and Paul warns of teachers who lead captive silly women. Same verb, four very different captivities.
TheologicalSignificance: The word asks whose prisoner I am, and I believe the answer is the whole point. Sin takes captives, false teachers take captives, and Christ takes captives too — the difference is that His captivity is freedom, because every thought brought under His rule is a thought finally set right.
RelatedTopics: Sin; Spiritual Warfare; Freedom; False Teaching
